cleanIntro: Caesar Guerini publishes one owner's manual for its whole over/under line, and it does not name individual models: it says its over-and-unders all function and operate in essentially the same way. Every step here is that book's general procedure, stated as the book states it. The book names the Woodlander nowhere, and the one model-specific section it prints — a fore-end tension screw on the Invictus action — is not carried here. The strip is three pieces: fore-end, barrels, and receiver with stock, and the book goes no further.

steps.title: Safety on S, muzzle somewhere safe
steps.action: Push the safety to S so the letter shows completely, and point the gun in a safe direction before your hand goes to the top lever.
steps.prose: Every step after this opens the action. Put the safety on first, before the breech is opened.
steps.quote: Put the safety in the “S” (on) position and point the shotgun in a safe direction.
steps.cite: Caesar Guerini Use and Maintenance Manual — Over-and-Under Shotguns — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — TO UNLOAD THE GUN, PDF p.11 (printed p.19)
steps.warn: Make sure the gun is not loaded before disassembling and cleaning it so that it will not fire accidentally.

steps.title: Top lever right, barrels down, shells out by hand
steps.action: Push the top lever to the right. Hold the receiver in your shooting hand, put the other hand palm down on top of the barrels at the front of the fore-end, and push down. The breech opens on its hinge and the extractors raise the shells a little so you can take them out by hand.
steps.prose: The ejectors only throw out fired hulls. An unfired shell stays in the chamber, raised on the extractor, until you take it out.
steps.quote: Push the top lever to the right, support the receiver with the shooting hand and with the other hand grasp the top of the barrels palm down at the front of the fore-end and push down.
steps.cite: Caesar Guerini Use and Maintenance Manual — Over-and-Under Shotguns — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — TO UNLOAD THE GUN, PDF p.11 (printed p.19)

steps.title: Both chambers checked empty before the strip starts
steps.action: With the action open, look into both chambers and confirm the gun is on safe and neither barrel holds a shell. This is the first line of Guerini's disassembly instructions.
steps.prose: An over/under has two chambers. If you only look into the bottom one, you can miss a shell in the top one.
steps.quote: Make certain the shotgun is on safe and the action open with shells removed from both barrels.
steps.cite: Caesar Guerini Use and Maintenance Manual — Over-and-Under Shotguns — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — DISASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, PDF p.12 (printed p.20)

steps.title: Breech closed and locked again
steps.action: Close the breech and check that the top lever has snapped back and engaged the barrels. The fore-end comes off with the gun closed, not open.
steps.prose: While the breech is closed, the locking bolt holds the barrels on as the fore-end comes off. If the gun is open with the fore-end off, nothing holds the barrels on.
steps.quote: Close the breech and make sure the top lever engages the barrels.
steps.cite: Caesar Guerini Use and Maintenance Manual — Over-and-Under Shotguns — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — DISASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, PDF p.12 (printed p.20)

steps.title: Fore-end latch down, fore-end off
steps.action: Press down on the fore-end latch and take the fore-end off the barrels.
steps.prose: The fore-end holds the barrels to the receiver when the breech opens. Once it is off, hold the barrels yourself.
steps.quote: Press down on the fore-end latch and remove the fore-end
steps.cite: Caesar Guerini Use and Maintenance Manual — Over-and-Under Shotguns — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — DISASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, PDF p.12 (printed p.20)

steps.title: Action open, barrels lifted off the receiver
steps.action: Keep hold of the barrels, open the action with the top lever, and lift the barrels off the receiver. The strip is now three pieces: fore-end, barrels, and receiver with stock. Guerini's disassembly stops here.
steps.prose: With the fore-end off, only your hand holds the barrels once the breech opens. Keep hold of them so the monoblock does not drop against the receiver face.
steps.quote: Open the action using the top lever, being careful to keep control of the barrels and carefully remove the barrels from the receiver
steps.cite: Caesar Guerini Use and Maintenance Manual — Over-and-Under Shotguns — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — DISASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS, PDF p.12 (printed p.20)

steps.title: Solvent patch through each bore, from the chamber end
steps.action: Wet a patch with bore solvent and push it through each bore from the chamber end. Let the solvent soak in while you clean the receiver.
steps.prose: Pushing from the chamber end sends the fouling out of the muzzle instead of back toward the action.
steps.quote: Wet a patch with bore cleaning solvent and wet the inside of each bore by pushing the wet patch through from the chamber end of the barrel.
steps.cite: Caesar Guerini Use and Maintenance Manual — Over-and-Under Shotguns — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — BARREL SET, PDF p.12 (printed p.20)

steps.title: Brush full strokes, then patches until one comes out clean
steps.action: Change to a brush and run it from the chamber end in full strokes, all the way through and back, never changing direction while the brush is still in the bore. Then run patches from the rear until one comes out clean, and finish with a patch lightly wet with lubricant or preservative.
steps.prose: The full-stroke rule is there so the brush is never reversed inside the bore. The last patch should leave a thin film on the steel, because shot-shell residue can corrode a bare bore.
steps.quote: Brush 5 to 10 full cycles (1 cycle = one stroke in and one stroke out).
steps.cite: Caesar Guerini Use and Maintenance Manual — Over-and-Under Shotguns — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — BARREL SET, PDF p.12 (printed p.20)

steps.title: Outside of the barrels wiped and covered with preservative
steps.action: Wipe moisture, dirt and carbon off the outside of both barrels, then coat the metal with a good preservative. Wipe off your fingerprints as you work.
steps.prose: Bluing does not stop rust. The acid in a fingerprint can start rust on blued steel.
steps.quote: Carefully wipe the outside of the barrels to remove any moisture, dirt, carbon or other residues from the bluing.
steps.cite: Caesar Guerini Use and Maintenance Manual — Over-and-Under Shotguns — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — BARREL SET, PDF p.12 (printed p.21)
steps.warn: Rust can and will occur if this step is neglected and this is NOT covered by warranty.

steps.title: A light coat of grease on the outside of each choke tube
steps.action: With a choke tube out of the barrel, put a light coat of protective grease around its outside before you screw it back in.
steps.prose: Firing pushes gas in behind the tube. Without grease, the outside of the tube corrodes and the tube can stick in the barrel.
steps.quote: we recommend covering the external circumference of the choke tube with a light quantity of protective grease.
steps.cite: Caesar Guerini Use and Maintenance Manual — Over-and-Under Shotguns — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — INSTALLATION AND REMOVAL OF CHOKE TUBES, PDF p.11 (printed p.18)

steps.title: Receiver brushed, solvent kept off the wood
steps.action: Brush residue, carbon and dirt off the receiver with a soft bristle brush and general-purpose solvent. Keep the solvent off the stock and fore-end, and do not let it run down inside the receiver. Let the receiver air dry, or blow it dry carefully.
steps.prose: Solvent that runs into the receiver or soaks into the wood does more harm than the dirt you were cleaning off.
steps.quote: The receiver should have any residue/carbon/ dirt removed with a soft bristle brush and general purpose solvent.
steps.cite: Caesar Guerini Use and Maintenance Manual — Over-and-Under Shotguns — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — STOCK, RECEIVER AND FORE-END GROUP, PDF p.12 (printed p.21)

steps.title: Wood wiped with a damp cloth, then linseed oil
steps.action: Wipe the dirt off the stock and fore-end with a cloth that is damp, not wet. Then rub in a small amount of boiled linseed oil, firmly, until no excess is left on the wood.
steps.prose: Oil put on over dirt traps the dirt under it. If oil is still standing on the stock, you used too much or did not rub it in long enough.
steps.quote: After the stock on the shotgun is cleaned it can be rubbed with boiled linseed oil
steps.cite: Caesar Guerini Use and Maintenance Manual — Over-and-Under Shotguns — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — STOCK, RECEIVER AND FORE-END GROUP, PDF p.12 (printed p.21)

steps.title: Thin film on the barrels, extra at the pivots, oil on the fore-end latch
steps.action: Give the whole barrel group a thin film of oil. Oil the inside of the receiver lightly, with a little extra where the barrels pivot. Oil the latch mechanism inside the fore-end at its specific points.
steps.prose: When Guerini says "extra lubricant", it means paying extra attention to those points, not oiling until it drips off the gun.
steps.quote: Lubricate only with a thin film over the entire group (enough to prevent rust).
steps.cite: Caesar Guerini Use and Maintenance Manual — Over-and-Under Shotguns — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — LUBRICATION INSTRUCTIONS, PDF p.12 (printed p.21)

deepAbsentReason: The book ends at the field strip. Its DISASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS (PDF p.12, printed p.20) take the gun down to fore-end, barrels, and receiver with stock, and stop there. Its other maintenance pages cover cleaning, lubrication, reassembly and adjustments: the DTS rib and stock comb, and the fore-end tension screw that only the Invictus has. It gives no procedure for the trigger group, ejectors or firing pins, or for removing the stock, so no deeper step is written here.

cleaning.name: BARREL SET
tasks: Solvent patch through each bore from the chamber end, left to soak
Bore brush from the chamber end, 5 to 10 full cycles, never reversed inside the bore
Patches from the rear until one comes out clean
A patch lightly wet with lubricant or preservative through each bore
Outside of the barrels wiped and covered with preservative

cleaning.name: CHOKE TUBES
tasks: A light coat of protective grease on the outside of each choke tube
Thread-cleaning tool on the choke key turned clockwise only

cleaning.name: RECEIVER, STOCK & FORE-END
tasks: Receiver brushed with a soft bristle brush and general-purpose solvent
Do not let solvent run onto the wood or down into the receiver
Stock and fore-end wiped with a damp, not wet, cloth
Boiled linseed oil rubbed in, no excess left

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: Thin film over the whole barrel group
Extra at the barrel pivot points and on the extractors
Inside of the receiver lightly, extra where the barrels pivot
The latch points inside the fore-end

reassembly: Set the locking blocks on the barrels into the inside of the receiver and make sure they are engaged. Then move the top lever to the right and close the breech.
⚠ The gun looks assembled now but is not. If the breech is opened before the fore-end is on, the barrels will come off the receiver.
Put the fore-end on the front of the receiver and push its front end toward the barrels until the fore-end catch button snaps in. Only then is it safe to open the barrels.
fncheck: With the gun empty and the fore-end on, open the breech with the top lever and close it again. The barrels should stay on the receiver, and the top lever should snap back to the left and lock the breech. Guerini's reassembly ends at the point where the fore-end is secured and the barrels are safe to open.
